title: Does Gross Salary Include Super? Understanding Your Hourly Rate, Annual Pay, and Award Entitlements
description: Wondering does gross salary include super? Learn how to convert hourly to annual pay, the role of awards, casual loading, and why super is paid on top.
salarySummary: For a full-time employee on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, working 38 hours a week, the annual gross salary is about $52,270 before tax and super.

faqs.a: No, gross salary does not include superannuation. Under Australian law, the super guarantee (currently 12% of ordinary earnings) is paid by the employer on top of your gross salary. Your gross salary is the amount before tax and before any super contributions are added. The Fair Work Ombudsman states that the minimum pay rate is the gross pay before tax is taken out, and super is a separate entitlement.

faqs.q: How do I convert an hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time position, we assume 38 hours per week. For example, $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,269.44 annual gross. If you work fewer or more hours, adjust accordingly. This formula gives a base estimate; actual pay may vary with overtime, penalties, or allowances.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage ($26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026) is the legal minimum for all employees not covered by an award or agreement. Most employees are covered by a modern award that sets higher minimum rates for their industry or occupation. Award rates can include penalty rates, allowances, and casual loading (typically 25% on top of the base rate). Always check the relevant award via the Fair Work Ombudsman’s Pay Calculator to ensure you’re being paid correctly.

bodyMarkdown:
## Does Gross Salary Include Super? A Clear Answer

If you’ve ever asked **does gross salary include super**, the short answer is no. In Australia, your gross salary is the amount you earn before tax and before any superannuation contributions. Super is paid by your employer on top of your gross salary, currently at 12% of your ordinary earnings (with a maximum contribution base of $270,830 for 2026–27). The Fair Work Ombudsman confirms that minimum pay rates are gross pay, and super is a separate entitlement. Understanding this distinction is crucial when comparing a salary offer or calculating your take-home pay.

## Converting Hourly to Annual Pay: The Formula

To estimate your annual gross salary, use this simple formula:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

We assume a standard full-time week of 38 hours, as defined by the National Employment Standards. For example, if you earn the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour:

- Weekly gross: $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.72 (matches the Fair Work figure of $1,004.90, a minor rounding difference)
- Fortnightly gross: $1,004.72 × 2 = $2,009.44
- Annual gross: $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,269.44

This formula works for any hourly rate. If you work part-time or casual, adjust the hours per week accordingly. Remember, this is a base estimate—it assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice.

### The Fortnightly View

Many people are paid fortnightly, so knowing your fortnightly gross helps with budgeting. For a $26.44/hour employee, the fortnight is about $2,009.44. For the average full-time adult ordinary time earnings of $2,083.70 per week (Australian Bureau of Statistics, May 2026), the fortnightly gross is about $4,167.40. [average pay](/) is the floor. However, most employees are covered by a modern award that sets higher minimum rates for their industry or occupation. Awards also include penalty rates for weekends, evenings, and overtime, as well as allowances. For example, a hospitality award might pay a higher base rate plus a 25% casual loading. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides a Pay Calculator to find the correct award rate.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. The casual minimum wage is $33.05 per hour (including loading). When using our calculator, you enter your base hourly rate, and a checkbox adds 25% casual loading on top. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

## Tax and Super: What Comes Off Your Gross Salary

From your gross salary, the Australian Taxation Office requires tax to be withheld. For 2026–27, the resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% of excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30% of excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37% of excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: $51,420 plus 45% of excess over $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (with reductions for low-income earners using 2025–26 thresholds).

Superannuation is not deducted from your gross salary—it is paid by your employer on top. The super guarantee is 12% of ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a $26.44/hour employee, the annual super is about $6,272 per year. [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) explains how salary packaging can affect your super.

## Important Assumptions

Our calculator provides an estimate only. It assumes:

- Same hourly rate every week
- No unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances
- No salary sacrifice
- Super at 12% of ordinary earnings, capped at the maximum contribution base
- Tax using 2026–27 resident rates with full tax-free threshold
- Medicare using 2025–26 single reduction thresholds (2026–27 not confirmed)

HELP loans, Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. For a precise determination, consult the Fair Work Ombudsman, Australian Taxation Office, or a qualified advisor.

## Why This Matters

Knowing whether a salary offer includes super is vital. Some employers quote a “total package” that includes super, but the base salary is what you’re paid before super. Always ask: “Does gross salary include super?” If the answer is yes, your actual cash salary is lower. Use our calculator to compare hourly rates and annual salaries accurately. [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) and [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) pages can help you understand your net income.
